headline: 85 detained as police raid 'drug parties' at addl DIG's house in Dhaka
summary: The house was reportedly used for frequent parties with loud music and drug use, leading to the Additional DIG being made an officer on special duty.
details: Police raided a rented house in Dhaka’s Khilkhet area owned by Additional Deputy Inspector General Abdullah Al Zahir, detaining 85 people.
The raid followed repeated complaints from neighbors who were weary of loud music, dancing, and alleged drug use occurring at least 20 days a month.
Authorities recovered alcohol, yaba, kush, and equipment for consuming drugs during the operation, according to Dhaka Metropolitan Police Uttara Division Deputy Commissioner Ilias Kabir.
Among those detained were university students, bankers, and 26 young women, as well as children of law enforcement personnel and officials.
The venue was reportedly listed on Airbnb and Travela, with Zahir as the host and Mahbubul Alam as co-host, running events since 2025.
Men were sentenced to one month in jail and a fine of Tk 1,000, while women were sentenced to 15 days and the fined Tk 500.
Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir has been made an officer on special duty (OSD) and attached to police headquarters.
Zahir claimed he did not organize the events and had appointed a manager to follow the rules, stating that he expected only 35 to 40 guests that day.
caption:

Authorities recovered alcohol, yaba, kush, and equipment for consuming drugs during the operation, according to Dhaka Metropolitan Police Uttara Division Deputy Commissioner Ilias Kabir.

Among those detained were university students, bankers, and 26 young women, as well as children of law enforcement personnel and officials.

The venue was reportedly listed on Airbnb and Travela, with Zahir as the host and Mahbubul Alam as co-host, running events since 2025.

Men were sentenced to one month in jail and a fine of Tk 1,000, while women were sentenced to 15 days and the fined Tk 500.

Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir has been made an officer on special duty (OSD) and attached to police headquarters.

Zahir claimed he did not organize the events and had appointed a manager to follow the rules, stating that he expected only 35 to 40 guests that day.

headline_marked: Global alert: [[Websites go dark worldwide]] to fix critical PHP security flaws
headline: Global alert: Websites go dark worldwide to fix critical PHP security flaws
summary: Government portals in Europe and elsewhere were taken offline as a precaution after AI-assisted hacking threats exposed critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language.
details: Government websites in Europe and other regions went offline on Wednesday as operators scrambled to fix critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language.
PHP powers roughly 75% of websites whose language can be identified, including the engine behind WordPress, which runs about 43% of all websites globally.
Agencies in the Netherlands, Finland, and Denmark took sites offline as a precaution, including the Port of Rotterdam, hospital websites, and national soccer association KNVB.
Cybersecurity experts warn that AI-assisted hacking campaigns could magnify the threat, allowing exploitation to happen instantly and on a massive scale.
The PHP developers released a fix on Wednesday, but security firms like Cloudflare and Wordfence warned that automatic updates may not apply the patch immediately.
The risk is particularly high for small websites and those on shared hosting, where owners lack direct control over the underlying servers to apply updates.
